title: One-Pot Chicken and Rice
seoTitle: One-Pot Chicken and Rice | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: One pot, hard to mess up
subtitle: One pot, hard to mess up
description: One pot, hard to mess up. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Brown sausage and chicken
steps.instruction: In a large Dutch oven, brown sliced sausage and chicken over medium-high. Remove — fond is flavor.

steps.title: Toast rice and simmer
steps.instruction: Sauté trinity vegetables, stir in rice 1 minute, add tomatoes, broth, and Cajun seasoning. Nestle meat back in. Simmer covered 25 minutes.

steps.title: Rest and fluff
steps.instruction: Off heat 10 minutes covered, then fluff. One-Pot Chicken and Rice should be moist but not soupy — add broth if rice is chalky.

steps.title: Serve from the pot
steps.instruction: Serve straight from the Dutch oven or transfer to a cambro on warm. Scrape the fond from the bottom — that's free flavor.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate One-Pot Chicken and Rice with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up One-Pot Chicken and Rice on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: One pot, hard to mess up. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
